sources.title: UK local authority and regional greenhouse gas emissions statistics collection
facts: DESNZ identifies this collection as the reliable consistent local and regional GHG series and states it covers CO2, CH4 and N2O but excludes fluorinated gases from local estimates.
Local-authority estimates are aggregate statistical allocations and are not cadastral parcel measurements.

sources.title: UK local authority and regional greenhouse gas emissions statistics 2005 to 2024
facts: The 2005-2024 DESNZ release uses nationally available datasets and covers local/regional GHG estimates, while aviation, shipping, military transport and F-gases are not allocated locally in this product.
A local-authority total or significant point-source map does not establish emissions for an individual land parcel.

sources.title: 2005 to 2024 UK local and regional greenhouse gas emissions technical report web accessible
facts: The technical report explains spatial disaggregation of GHGI CO2, CH4 and N2O by local authority, including proxy distributions, agriculture, waste and uncertainty.
Spatial disaggregation and proxy allocation are modelled estimates and must not be promoted to direct parcel observations.

sources.title: 2005 to 2024 UK local and regional greenhouse gas emissions statistical release web accessible
facts: DESNZ reports territorial local-area estimates with special allocation rules for energy supply and waste and documents recalculation of 2005-2023 history under 2024 methods.
Recalculated historical local-area data must preserve method/version context and cannot be treated as parcel-bound measurement.

sources.title: Mapping GHG emissions and removals for LULUCF web accessible
facts: The LULUCF methodology covers forestry, peatland, cropland/grassland mineral soil change, settlements, bioenergy crops, uncertainty and recalculations.
Mapped LULUCF emissions/removals at local or grid scales are not automatically attributable to a cadastral parcel without geometry and method binding.

sources.title: UK greenhouse gas emissions local authority and regional National Data Library
facts: The National Data Library catalogue exposes the 2005-2024 local-authority GHG CSV and supporting methodology resources.
Catalogue metadata and local-authority CSV rows are aggregate statistical evidence rather than direct parcel measurements.

sources.title: Local authority greenhouse gas emissions 2025 estimates announcement
facts: DESNZ lists the 2025 local-authority GHG estimates for a provisional June 2027 release.
Future-release metadata contains no observed 2025 local-authority values and must not be used as current measurement.

sources.title: Farm practices survey February 2026
facts: Defra's 2026 Farm Practices Survey covers nutrient management, anaerobic digestion, emissions, manure/slurry, grassland and livestock practices in England.
Survey proportions describe holdings and practices; they are not measured GHG quantities for individual farms or parcels.

sources.title: Farm Practices Survey 2026 introduction
facts: The introduction reports headline practice shares such as nutrient plans, anaerobic digestion and emissions-reduction actions across English holdings.
A proportion of holdings adopting a practice must not be converted directly to emissions reductions or parcel values.

sources.title: Farm Practices Survey 2026 emissions
facts: Defra reports farmer attitudes and actions related to GHG mitigation, including manure/slurry efficiency and methane-suppressing feed use.
Self-reported mitigation practice or attitude is not a quantified observed farm or parcel emissions result.

sources.title: Farm Practices Survey 2026 metadata
facts: The survey sampled about 7,000 targeted English holdings with an approximately 22% response rate and applies activity thresholds.
Survey design and weights govern representativeness; sample responses cannot be treated as direct emissions measurements.

sources.title: Farm practices survey statistical dataset and time series
facts: Defra's statistical dataset provides Farm Practices Survey time-series results from 2011 through 2026.
Time-series practice indicators are survey evidence, not physical GHG inventories for individual holdings.

sources.title: Farm Practices Survey 2026 anaerobic digestion
facts: Defra reports 15% of farms processing waste, crops or feedstocks by anaerobic digestion in 2026 and distinguishes material types.
Adoption of anaerobic digestion or feedstock share does not itself quantify methane capture, leakage or net GHG emissions.

sources.title: Farm Practices Survey 2026 nutrient management
facts: Defra reports nutrient-management plans, nutrient testing, manure-management plans and soil monitoring practices.
Nutrient-management practice evidence may affect emissions drivers but is not a measured N2O parcel value.

sources.title: Farm Practices Survey 2026 manure and slurry storage
facts: The survey reports manure and slurry storage methods and notes their relevance to air and water environmental risks.
A storage method category is activity/practice evidence and does not directly establish methane or nitrous-oxide emissions.

sources.title: Farm Practices Survey 2026 fertiliser manure and slurry spreaders
facts: Defra reports spreading and spreader-calibration practices, including that 69% of relevant farmers calibrated manure/slurry spreaders at least some of the time in 2026.
Spreading/calibration practice is activity evidence; emissions require supported rates, factors, soils, timing and scope.

sources.title: Farm Practices Survey 2026 grassland and grazing
facts: Defra reports clover-mix and high-sugar-grass practices that may improve production efficiency and reduce inputs or emissions intensity.
A practice with mitigation potential is not an observed absolute GHG reduction for a holding or parcel.

sources.title: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025
facts: Defra's annual Agriculture in the UK publication covers production, livestock, land use, inputs and agri-environment statistics.
Agricultural sector statistics are national/industry evidence and must not be assigned directly to individual parcels.

sources.title: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025 chapter 11 Agri-environment
facts: Defra reports agriculture accounted for about 59% of UK N2O and 49% of methane emissions in 2024 and documents inventory revisions.
National agricultural shares and totals do not establish emissions for a specific farm or parcel.

sources.title: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025 release announcement
facts: The accredited-statistics announcement records the confirmed 9 July 2026 release timing for Agriculture in the UK 2025.
Release-calendar metadata is provenance/currentity evidence and not an emissions observation.

sources.title: UK Informative Inventory Report 1990 to 2024
facts: NAEI's 1990-2024 Informative Inventory Report documents UK air-emissions inventory methods and includes a correction note about a mileage-data statement.
Inventory methodology/currentity evidence supports provenance but is not a parcel-level observation.

sources.title: T24 anaerobic digestion on farms waste exemption
facts: Environment Agency T24 guidance sets waste quantities and conditions for on-farm anaerobic digestion and burning resulting biogas.
An exemption limit or permitted treatment quantity is regulatory scope and not a GHG emissions measurement.

sources.title: SR2021 No 8 on-farm anaerobic digestion installation rules
facts: Environment Agency standard rules cover operations, emissions and monitoring for qualifying on-farm anaerobic-digestion installations.
A standard-rule permit framework defines controls but does not itself prove measured methane leakage or parcel emissions.

sources.title: Organic farming statistics 2025
facts: Defra publishes annual UK and England statistics on organic crops, land and livestock.
Organic status, area or livestock counts are activity/context data and do not directly quantify GHG emissions.

sources.title: ONS atmospheric greenhouse gases by industry and gas provisional edition
facts: ONS provisional Environmental Accounts provide top-level greenhouse-gas estimates and explicitly distinguish provisional revisions from corrections.
Provisional residence-basis industry estimates must remain versioned and are not parcel-level territorial measurements.
